# Feature: Onboarding, Health & Credentials

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-071
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

This feature gives a person who never opens a terminal three things in the Yantra app:

- **Onboarding.** A first-run setup that produces the same `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` that
  terminal `yantra init` produces for the same answers.
- **Health.** A screen that shows every `yantra doctor` check, and offers a one-click fix only
  where Yantra has a real way to perform it.
- **Credentials.** Credentials the user can set and remove but never read back.

These are the last three bespoke parity surfaces in plan_ui §12 (`init`, `doctor`, `secret`). After
this feature, every `init`, `doctor` and `secret` subcommand maps to an app surface, so the parity
manifest no longer needs a placeholder for them (memory → General, CLI ↔ app parity).

The feature's whole security posture follows plan_ui D2 and §7:

- secret values are written **in the host process** through the same core keychain function that
  `yantra secret set` uses;
- they never appear in any process's argv;
- after submission they never come back to the app.

Plan references: §1, D2, D5, D13, D15, D16, §6 (execution classes: `init` adapter, `doctor`
`read`/`run`, `secret` `in-process-secure`), §7 Secrets, §8 Reliability matrix (possible orphans),
§9, §10 Security suite, §11 host log, §12 FEAT-071, §8 Sequencing (FEAT-071 after FEAT-070).

### Acceptance (from plan_ui §12, verbatim intent)

1. Onboarding produces the same `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` as terminal `init` for the same
   answers.
2. Every `doctor` check renders.
3. Outbound canary scans pass for set, list and remove.
4. No credential value ever reaches the app after submission.
5. No credential appears in any process's argv.

### Decisions recorded by this spec

- **SD-1: Answers are collected in the app first and submitted once.** The browser answer collector
  is a _pre-answered_ collector. The app renders the `init` service's question catalog, gathers
  every answer locally, and submits one `onboarding.submit` request. The host then runs the shared
  `init` service in-process with a collector that answers each question from that payload.
  - If the service asks a question the payload does not answer, the submission fails closed with
    `missing_answer {question_id}`. It never falls back to a default.
  - Why this design: a question-by-question RPC dialogue would hold a half-written installation
    open across a window that can close at any moment. It would also create a second secret
    channel.
- **SD-2: Questions are explicit, with no inference.**
  - The app never pre-selects an answer from the environment. For example, it does not pre-select
    "environment variable" because `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (memory: prefer explicit user grants).
  - Each question has no selection until the user picks one. The location grant in particular must
    be answered explicitly.
  - Defaults shown are the terminal's literal defaults (for example, the model ID
    `claude-opus-4-7`). They appear as editable initial values, never as silent choices.
  - **Skippable:**
    - Every optional question has the same `skip` choice the terminal offers.
    - The whole flow has **Not now**, which writes nothing. While `config.yaml` is absent, a
      non-modal "Yantra isn't set up yet — Set up" banner shows on Mission.
    - No preference is added to remember the dismissal. That avoids a new `profile.yaml` key, and
      memory forbids dead controls.
- **SD-3: The data directory is shown, not changed.** See DEVIATION-1.
- **SD-4: Remediation actions are a declared catalog, checked by a test.**
  - Doctor's `fixHint` stays prose, and `doctor --json` is unchanged.
  - Health maps a check, its status and its details to an action through a catalog. Each catalog
    entry declares the registry command path or app route it uses, plus the evidence that this
    action fixes the condition.
  - A test asserts that every action resolves. A check with no engineered path renders its prose
    hint and no button.
  - This applies the memory rule "advice may only name a move the engine has an engineered path
    for".
- **SD-5: Health reads run in-process; only the smoke check uses a worker.**
  - `doctor` (without `--agent-smoke`) is `read` class, so Health calls `read.doctor` in the host.
  - `doctor --agent-smoke` is `run` class. It goes through `command.invoke` like any run (D4 slot,
    D11 invocation record) and appears in the Ledger.
- **SD-6: Removing a credential that something references asks first.**
  - `secret rm` on a key that `config.yaml` references (a model `api_key` or `search.<p>.api_key`)
    shows the referencing entries and requires explicit confirmation.
  - The CLI's behavior and output are unchanged.

> **DEVIATION-1 (awaiting confirmation): Onboarding does not let the user pick the storage
> location while the app is running.**
>
> **What the plan says.** plan_ui §12 lists "storage" among the onboarding answers.
>
> **Why that conflicts with D15.** Choosing a data directory in `init` writes `paths.data_dir`,
> which relocates the directory that holds the live host's `host.lock`, `slots.lock`,
> `invocations/` and sockets. D15 says relocation "cannot run under a live host", and the
> `config data-dir` guard refuses it for exactly this reason. If the app's `init` wrote a different
> `paths.data_dir`, the next CLI process would no longer find the host lock, and a second host
> could start.
>
> **What this spec does instead.**
>
> - The storage question renders read-only. It shows the current effective location and the D15
>   steps for changing it: close the app, run `yantra init --reset` or
>   `yantra config data-dir <path>` in a terminal, then run `yantra ui`.
> - The submitted answer is the value `config.yaml` already holds (`null` on a first run).
> - The host also refuses any submission whose resulting `paths.data_dir` differs from the live
>   one, with `relocation_requires_terminal`.
>
> **Effect on acceptance 1.** It still holds for every answer set the app can produce.
>
> **Possible later fix.** A host-assisted relocation (the host exits and relaunches against the new
> location) is in `TODO.md`.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

`.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature adds no database tables; everything is
filesystem- or keychain-backed (memory → Project Structure). The entities below are protocol
(Zod) or in-process shapes.

### Entities & Attributes

- **InitQuestion** (`@yantra/protocol`, `schemas/init-questions.ts`; data, importable by
  `apps/web`). This is the one catalog that both the terminal wizard and the app render. If
  FEAT-072's `init` service already exposes equivalent question descriptors, those descriptors
  _are_ this catalog; move them to protocol unchanged rather than duplicating them.
  - `id` (enum: `provider`, `credential_source`, `credential_env_name`, `credential_secret`,
    `model_id`, `ollama_base_url`, `search_key_provider`, `search_key_secret`, `data_dir`,
    `context_location`, `context_city`). Unique, NOT NULL.
  - `kind` (`select | text | secret | confirm`). `secret` maps to the FEAT-062 `secret-input` kind.
  - `message` (string). The exact terminal prompt text, for example `'Model provider'`,
    `'Credential source'` or the `LOCATION_QUESTION` sentence. NOT NULL.
  - `choices` (readonly string[] | null). Required for `select`, for example
    `['anthropic','ollama','none']` or `['environment variable','keychain','skip']`.
  - `initial` (string | null). The terminal's literal initial value, for example
    `'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'`, `'claude-opus-4-7'` or `'http://localhost:11434'`. It is never derived
    from the environment.
  - `optional` (boolean). True when the terminal accepts skip or blank.
  - `when` (a closed discriminated union over earlier answers, such as
    `{question:'provider', in:['anthropic','ollama']}`). Data, not a function, so the app and the
    terminal evaluate it identically.
  - `section` (`model | search | storage | context`). Groups questions into onboarding steps.
- **InitAnswers** (`@yantra/protocol`, Zod; the request half of `onboarding.submit`):
  - `answers` (record keyed by `InitQuestion.id`, value `string | boolean | null`). Never contains a
    `secret`-kind value.
  - `secrets` (`{credential_secret?: string, search_key_secret?: string}`). Each value is a
    non-empty string of at most 8 KiB. This is the only part of the payload that carries values. It
    is excluded from logging by schema-level redaction metadata.
  - `reset` (boolean, default `false`). Mirrors `init --reset`.
  - `invocation_id` (string). Idempotency key, the same convention as D11. A repeat returns the
    first result.
- **OnboardingStatus** (the `read.onboarding_status` response):
  - `config_exists`, `profile_exists` (boolean).
  - `config_path`, `profile_path` (absolute paths from `paths.ts`).
  - `data_dir {effective, source, configured}`. `configured` is the current `paths.data_dir`
    value, or `null`.
  - `keychain_available` (boolean). A capability fact, not an inference: it decides whether the
    `keychain` choice is enabled, with the reason and remedy.
- **OnboardingResult** (the `onboarding.submit` response; values never echoed):
  - `status` (`written | already_initialized`).
  - `config_path`, `profile_path`, and `profile_written` (boolean).
  - `provider` (`anthropic | ollama | none`), the same field `init --json` emits.
  - `search_key` (`skipped | stored | manual`), plus `command` when `manual`.
  - `location_shared` (boolean).
  - Errors are typed: `missing_answer {question_id}`, `invalid_answer {question_id, reason}`,
    `keychain_unavailable {remedy}`, `relocation_requires_terminal {steps}`,
    `busy {holder}` (D14), and `already_initialized` (submitted without `reset` while `config.yaml`
    exists).
- **CredentialRow** (core `secrets/credential-service.ts`; the `secret.list` response):
  - `key` (string), the keychain account or display key, matching today's `secret list`.
  - `source` (`keychain | env | absent`).
  - `referenced_by` (readonly `{kind: 'model' | 'search', id: string, ref: ConfigRefDisplay}[]`).
    New, and used only by the app; the CLI projection drops it.
  - `ConfigRefDisplay` = `{kind: 'secret', key} | {kind: 'env', name}`. This is the reference
    ProtectedValue shows. It never carries a value or a length.
- **CredentialListResult**: `{available: boolean, remedy: string | null, rows: CredentialRow[]}`.
- **SecretSetRequest** / **SecretRemoveRequest** (RPC): `{key, value}` and `{key}`.
  - `key` is validated by `parseConfigRef('${secret:<key>}')`.
  - `value` is non-empty and at most 8 KiB.
  - Responses: `{status: 'set', key}` and `{status: 'removed' | 'absent', key}`. They never contain
    `value`.
- **DoctorCheckId** (`@yantra/protocol`). The closed list of every check ID `doctor` can emit:
  - from core: `browser.selection`, `browser.compatibility`, `browser.managed`, `datadir.writable`,
    `datadir.permissions`, `cachedir.writable`, `keychain.reachable`, `indexdb.writable`;
  - from agent: `agent.model`, `agent.credentials`, `agent.budgets`;
  - from the CLI configuration checks: `config.valid`, `paths.resolved`, `ethics.robots`,
    `search.tavily.api-key`, `search.brave.api-key`, `search.provider`.

  `CHECK_TITLES` in `doctor.ts` is typed `satisfies Record<DoctorCheckId, string>`, and a runtime
  test asserts the same set (memory: package typecheck does not cover tests).

- **DoctorResult** (`@yantra/protocol` Zod). The `doctor --json` shape that already exists as
  `DoctorRenderResult` in `apps/cli/src/render/types.ts`. Add it only if FEAT-062 or FEAT-070 have
  not already defined it (TODO "JSON output schemas for read-class commands"). It is
  byte-compatible with today's output.
- **RemediationAction** (`apps/web`, the Health catalog). One of:
  - `{kind: 'invoke', path: readonly string[], argv: readonly string[]}`, a registry command run
    through `command.invoke`;
  - `{kind: 'navigate', route: RouteId, params: Record<string, string>}`, for example Credentials
    with `key=tavily.api_key`, Preferences focused on a key, Settings → Browser, or Settings →
    Installation;
  - `{kind: 'text'}`, prose only.

  Each catalog entry is
  `{check: DoctorCheckId, when: {status: readonly ('warn' | 'fail')[], details?: closed predicate}, action, label, evidence: string}`.
  `evidence` names the code path that makes the action fix the condition.

- **HostEnvironmentInfo** (the `read.host_status` response, or an extension of FEAT-065's existing
  host status read):
  - `host_started_at` and `env_captured_at` (ISO strings);
  - `yantra_version` and `host_pid`.

  No environment names or values.

- **PossibleOrphan** (the `read.possible_orphans` response, from FEAT-064's retained ownership
  records whose identity verdict is `unknown`):
  - `run_id`, `pid`, `recorded_start_token_present` (boolean), `executable` (basename only),
    `recorded_at`, and `reason` (`identity_unverifiable`).

  Read-only. It never triggers termination (memory → Architecture: `unknown` is never `dead`).

### Relationships

- InitQuestion 1:N InitQuestion through `when` (a question depends on earlier answers; the graph is
  acyclic and checked by a test).
- InitAnswers N:1 InitQuestion catalog (keys must be catalog IDs; extra keys are rejected).
- CredentialRow 1:N `referenced_by` entries, derived from `config.yaml` model and search
  references.
- RemediationAction N:1 DoctorCheckId; `invoke` actions N:1 registry command path; `navigate`
  actions N:1 app route.
- PossibleOrphan N:1 run (`run_id`), through FEAT-064's ownership record.

### Indexes & Constraints

- InitQuestion `id` is unique; `when` references only earlier question IDs.
- `InitAnswers.answers` must not contain a key whose question kind is `secret`. Schema refinement
  rejects it, so a secret cannot travel in the loggable half.
- Every `DoctorCheckId` has at least one catalog entry, or an explicit `{kind: 'text'}` entry with a
  reason.
- Every `invoke` path exists in the FEAT-062 registry, with class `read`, `run` or `exclusive`,
  never `exemption`.
- Every `navigate` route exists in the app route tree.

## 4. Dependencies

Must be implemented first (plan_ui §8 Sequencing: FEAT-071 after FEAT-070):

- **FEAT-061 Drshya Foundations.** TextField, Dialog, Switch, Select, Disclosure, Button, Toast
  primitives, tokens, icon registry, gallery and axe harness.
- **FEAT-062 Command Registry.** Registry entries for `init`, `doctor`, `secret`; the `secret-input`
  kind; `danger` on `secret rm`; execution classes (`doctor` option-dependent).
- **FEAT-072 Command Handler Seams.** The `init` application service with a pluggable answer
  collector; D14 locks for `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` with unique temporary files.
  `saveProfile` still writes a fixed `<path>.tmp` today, which FEAT-072 removes.
- **FEAT-063 / FEAT-064.** The run socket, worker entry and ownership records. These carry the
  agent-smoke run and are the source of possible orphans.
- **FEAT-065 App Host.** Sessions and per-window capability, JSON-RPC dispatcher, `read.*`
  in-process reads, `command.invoke`, the host log, environment capture time, and the security
  suite harness.
- **FEAT-066 Run Results & Audit.** The ProtectedValue and EventInspector instruments, and the run
  result route the smoke run links to.
- **FEAT-067 Mission.** The Mission page that hosts the setup banner, and the run-state store used
  to follow the smoke run.
- **FEAT-070 Parity, Palette & Generated Surfaces.** The parity manifest and behavior test; Settings
  → Preferences, Models, Browser and Installation surfaces that `navigate` remediations target;
  palette dispatch to adapters.

Infrastructure already present: `createKeychainProvider` and `YANTRA_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE`
(`packages/core/src/secrets/keychain.ts`), `parseConfigRef`, `redactConfigRefs`, `loadConfig`,
`saveProfile`, core `doctor()`, `runAgentDiagnostics`, `runAgentSmoke`, and `paths.ts`.

No new third-party dependency. Everything used is in plan_ui §3, approved and pinned by FEAT-061
and FEAT-065.

**STUB policy.** If FEAT-064 ships no read over retained ownership records, TASK-009 adds the
read-only `possible-orphans.ts` over FEAT-064's record format. It never adds cleanup.

### TASK-001: Shared core credential service; `yantra secret` delegates to it with unchanged output

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `packages/core/src/secrets/credential-service.ts`, with an injected `KeychainProvider`,
    `env` and config loader:
    - `validateCredentialKey(key)`, using `parseConfigRef('${secret:<key>}')`;
    - `setCredential({key, value})`. It rejects an empty value or one over 8 KiB, requires
      `isAvailable()`, and calls `keychain.set(YANTRA_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE, key, value)`;
    - `removeCredential({key})`, returning `removed | absent`;
    - `listCredentials()`, returning `CredentialListResult`. Rows merge exactly as `runList` does
      today (keychain accounts, the `tavily`/`brave` search refs, model refs), plus
      `referenced_by`.

    `secret.ts:unavailable`).

### TASK-002: Credentials surface: write-only set, names-only list, guarded remove, all in-process

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Protocol.** `schemas/credentials.ts` with the request and response schemas in §2; `value`
    carries Zod `.describe('secret')` metadata, which the host's log redactor keys on.
  - **Host.** `credentials.ts` handlers registered on FEAT-065's dispatcher:
    - `secret.set` calls `setCredential` in the host process (D2 exception) and never touches
      `command.invoke` or any spawn helper;
    - `secret.rm` and `secret.list` call the service.
    - Every handler requires the window capability (FEAT-065 middleware).
    - Responses never include `value`.
    - JSON-RPC error objects carry `{code, message, remediation}` only, never params.
    - Add `secret.set` and `onboarding.submit` to the host's param-redaction list, so a request is
      logged as `{method, key}`.
    - On success, the host log records `credential_changed {op: 'set' | 'rm', key}` (§11).
  - **`packages/ui` SecretField.** A React Aria `TextField` with `type=password`,
    `autoComplete="off"`, `spellCheck={false}`, and no reveal toggle. It holds the value in an
    uncontrolled ref, not React state. The `onSubmit(value)` callback receives it once, and the
    field clears synchronously afterwards. It shows "Stored values can't be viewed — set a new one
    to replace it."
  - **`apps/web` Credentials route (`/settings/credentials`).**
    - A table of `rows`: key, source badge (CLI words: `keychain`/`env`/`absent`), and
      "Used by". Each `referenced_by` reference renders with **ProtectedValue** (FEAT-066), which
      shows `${secret:key}` or `${env:NAME}`, never a value or its length.
    - Set or Replace opens `set-credential-dialog`: the key field (validated by
      `validateCredentialKey` rules mirrored from protocol) and the SecretField. Submit sends
      `secret.set` and shows a toast "Stored <key>."
    - The key can be prefilled from a route param, which is how Health and palette remediations
      land here.
    - Remove opens `remove-credential-dialog`. When `referenced_by` is non-empty, it lists the

### TASK-004: Browser answer collector and in-process `onboarding.submit`, file-equivalent to terminal `init`

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Add `createPreAnsweredCollector(answers, secrets)` to FEAT-072's `init` service.
    - It answers each catalog question the service asks from `answers` or `secrets`.
    - A question that applies but is absent throws `missing_answer {question_id}`.
    - A value outside a `select`'s choices throws `invalid_answer`.
  - **Host handlers:**
    - `read.onboarding_status` returns `OnboardingStatus`. It reads `configPath()`,
      `profilePath()`, `storageDirSources()` and the configured `paths.data_dir` from
      `loadConfig()` when the file exists, and probes `keychain.isAvailable()`.
    - `onboarding.submit` validates `InitAnswers`, then checks, in order:
      1. **Idempotency.** A repeated `invocation_id` returns the stored `OnboardingResult`, kept in
         memory for the host's lifetime and never containing secrets.
      2. **Existing installation.** If `config.yaml` exists and `reset` is false, return
         `already_initialized`, matching terminal `init`.
      3. **Relocation guard (DEVIATION-1).** If `answers.data_dir` differs from the configured
         value, return `relocation_requires_terminal`, with the D15 steps as data
         (`['Close every Yantra window', 'Run yantra init --reset or yantra config data-dir <path>', 'Run yantra ui']`).
      4. **Run.** Run the `init` service in-process with the pre-answered collector, under
         FEAT-072's `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` locks. Map a busy lock to `busy {holder}`
         (D14).
    - Keychain writes for `credential_secret` and `search_key_secret` happen in-process through
      the same calls the wizard makes. With the keychain unavailable:
      - the credential step yields `keychain_unavailable`, as the terminal throws;
      - the search step yields `search_key: manual` with the `yantra secret set` command, as the
        terminal does.
    - Return `OnboardingResult`, with no values. After success, invalidate the host's in-process
      read caches for config and profile, so Settings surfaces refresh.
    - Host log: `onboarding_submitted {status, provider, search_key, profile_written, reset}`. It
      never records answers' free text (the city) or secrets.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth.**
  - Every RPC in this feature requires FEAT-065's authenticated session cookie **and** per-window
    capability. Mutations (`secret.set`, `secret.rm`, `onboarding.submit`) also arrive only over
    the authenticated WebSocket with the exact `Origin` check.
  - Request size is capped at 1 MiB by the host, and secret values at 8 KiB by schema.
  - Credential writes and onboarding run in the host process (D2 exception), never through
    `command.invoke`, so no worker argv can carry a value. The agent smoke is the only path here
    that spawns a worker, and its argv holds options only.
- **Secrets.**
  - Values exist only in the inbound request, the host handler's local variables, and the OS
    keychain.
  - Every response, error, log line, query cache entry and DOM state after submit is
    canary-scanned (TASK-002, TASK-004, TASK-010).
  - ProtectedValue shows references, never values or lengths.
  - `credential-service.ts` owns validation, so the CLI and the app cannot diverge (memory: no
    validation grammar duplicated across layers). The app's client-side key check is UX only; the
    host re-validates.
- **Error Handling.**
  - Typed errors with safe, actionable remediation (memory → Coding Standards). Exit-code mapping
    is preserved for the CLI: 1 validation, 3 environment, including keychain unavailable and
    `busy`.
  - JSON-RPC errors carry `{code, message, remediation}` and never the request params.
  - A lock conflict is `busy` with the holder description, never a silent overwrite (D14).
  - A doctor sub-check failure is reported as that check's `fail` row; Health never fails as a
    page (per-item resilience, as in FEAT-066).
  - The remediation catalog offers only engineered actions (SD-4).
- **Logging.**
  - Host log (§11) adds `onboarding_submitted {status, provider, search_key, profile_written, reset}`,
    `credential_changed {op, key}`, and the existing lock-busy line. It never records secret
    values, free-text answers (city), launch codes, capabilities or environment values.
  - The params redactor keys on schema metadata, so a new secret field is redacted by declaration.
  - Core credential-service logs are at debug level with Pino `redact` covering `value`.
  - The agent smoke's own run directory logging is unchanged (FEAT-022).
- **Consistency and parity.**
  - Product words are the CLI's: `keychain`/`env`/`absent`, `ok`/`warn`/`fail`,
    `passed`/`failed`/`aborted`.
  - Onboarding questions come from the one catalog the terminal also renders. CLI output for
    `init`, `doctor` and `secret` is byte-identical before and after this feature.
- **Accessibility.**
  - All three surfaces are axe-clean in light and dark, Glass and Solid.
  - The onboarding flow and the credential dialogs work by keyboard alone; focus returns to the
    invoking control when a dialog closes.
  - Live updates (the smoke run, re-run checks) announce through the polite region only (§9).
